messages:
elaine-cs: Heads-up — Acme integration just escalated. Their ingestion pipeline fails intermittently when we return structured JSON in streaming mode. They pasted a parse error: "SyntaxError: Unexpected token \\ in JSON at position 127"

jess-support: Ack. Do we have a request id or example response chunk?

elaine-cs: Provided request id: req_01H9ZX0B. Repro snippet they sent (curl to our API):

curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"...","mode":"structured","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

They get streaming chunks like:

data: {"id":"req_01H9ZX0B","chunk":"{\"items\":[\"line1 \\nline2\"]}"}

data: {"id":"req_01H9ZX0B","chunk":"{\"items\":[\"more\"]}"}

Notice the inner JSON (the value of "chunk") contains escaped newlines (\\n) and escaped quotes. Customer's consumer expects to parse the concatenated payload into a final JSON object but gets double-escaped backslashes, then JSON.parse fails.

liam-eng-ml: That looks like we're serializing twice: once to produce the structured payload, then again when wrapping for SSE/stream framing. Can you paste the server-side log for that request id?

omar-sre: I pulled logs. Snippet from stream serializer at ~2025-07-14T19:03:21Z:

[INFO] req=req_01H9ZX0B serializer=stream_wrapper: framing payload: "{"chunk": "{\"items\": [\"line1 \\nline2\"]}"}"

There is an extra JSON.stringify in the stream_wrapper path. We're escaping inner JSON when we should be sending raw bytes as chunk content.

jess-support: Customer also reported spike in latency around the same time (p95 +200ms) and some partial responses where their parser aborted mid-stream. Could that be from our retries or buffering?

omar-sre: Buffering + stringify could increase serialized size and trigger multiple flushes. We'll look at Nagle/coalescing and the streaming flush logic.

liam-eng-ml: For triage: two actionable items — (1) immediate customer workaround, (2) fix in runtime. Workaround = set "stream": false or have them do a post-processing pass to replace \\n -> 
 and unescape quotes, but that's yuk. Recommend non-streaming until we patch.

ana-product: Can we push a short-term patch that avoids double-stringify for structured mode when stream=true? Also need test coverage for nested escaping.

omar-sre: I'll open a rollback-safe canary. Deploy bot, can you spin canary?

deploy-bot: @omar-sre canary deployment started: canary-esc-1755559999 -> 3 nodes in us-west2, health checks OK.

liam-eng-ml: Proposed fix: in stream_wrapper, detect if payload chunk is already a JSON string (starts with "{\" or \[) and then embed raw bytes rather than JSON.stringify. Also add unit test: simulate streaming structured content with internal strings containing 
, 	, quotes, unicode (e.g.,  ) and assert single-layer escaping.

elaine-cs: Customer wants ETA. Can we give a quick timeline?

omar-sre: Hotfix timeline: patch branch + tests in 1–2 hours, quick canary within 30min after merge, full roll 1–2 hours after canary if healthy. I'll also add a temporary flag on the API to force "stream_raw_chunks":true for select customers.

jess-support: I'll tell Acme to flip to non-stream for now and offer a temporary feature flag if they want to try canary. Provide them safe parsing example: parse each SSE data line, extract the "chunk" field and then call JSON.parse once on that extracted string (after replacing \\n -> 
 if needed). Example pseudo: 

```js
// on SSE line arrival
const payload = JSON.parse(sseLine.slice(6)); // strip 'data: '
const inner = payload.chunk;
const obj = JSON.parse(inner);
```

liam-eng-ml: Note: the above only works if the inner string is single-escaped. With double-escaping the inner still contains \\n sequences; parsing twice yields literal backslashes. We'll fix server-side.

ana-product: Add to release notes and mark as P1 for structured-streaming. Also add an eval test in Redwood Optimize to catch regressions.

elaine-cs: Customer appreciative of quick turnaround. They sent additional sample with unicode and emojis that currently get \uXXXX escapes then extra backslashing. I'll attach in the ticket.

omar-sre: Action items assigned: omar-sre -> patch stream_wrapper (hotfix), liam-eng-ml -> unit + integration tests, jess-support -> customer comms + flag, deploy-bot -> canary rollout. I'll update thread with PR link.

deploy-bot: canary healthy for 10m; no errors observed on canary logs for req_01H9ZX0B reproduction.

liam-eng-ml: Merged and promoted after canary. Please verify customer parsing.

elaine-cs: Confirmed with Acme — parser succeeds, no more Unexpected token errors. They reported lower latency on subsequent runs too. :tada:

ana-product: We'll schedule a follow-up to add a structured-mode streaming contract test to CI and document recommended client parsing patterns.

jess-support: Closing loop with customer and adding postmortem into #postmortems. Thanks team!
